# **5 Best Labguru Alternatives & Competitors in 2026**

A lab can usually manage things without much trouble when most of the work happens at one location. It gets different when samples start coming in from collection centres, other branches, or outside referrals. There is suddenly more to keep track of. Staff have to check where samples are, which tests are pending, whether results are ready, and whether a report has been checked before it is sent. With several samples moving through the lab at the same time, even a small delay can mean another follow-up.

This can become more noticeable as the lab adds more analysers and starts working with more referring doctors. Staff may have to check pending results, look into delayed reports, or confirm whether something has already been sent. None of these tasks take much time on their own, but doing them throughout the day can take up a fair amount of staff time. For a lab dealing with this regularly, it may be useful to compare other lab management systems and see what they handle differently.

 For diagnostic and pathology labs, choosing a lab management system is not only about handling samples. As operations grow, things such as analyser connectivity, report approval, billing, collection centre management, inventory, and work from multiple locations also become important. This guide looks at five Labguru alternatives that diagnostic labs can consider in 2026, along with the areas they cover and where they may have limitations.

## **How We Compared Labguru Alternatives**

We checked all five alternatives against the same set of requirements. We focused on things that matter when a lab is deciding whether to move to a new system, including workflow fit, ease of use, integrations, automation, customisation, reporting, implementation, data migration and export, scalability, user access, support, security, audit trails, and pricing.

We started with the vendors’ own websites and product documentation, then checked G2, Capterra, SoftwareSuggest, and Techjockey for independent information. The research was conducted in October 2026\.

Ratings were considered, but they were not the basis for comparing the software. We also looked at the type of laboratory each platform can support and how well it fits the way teams work. And when a vendor had not clearly mentioned a feature, integration, price, or compliance detail, we did not assume it was available.

## **A Closer Look at the Labguru Alternatives**

### **1\. Healthray**

![][image1]  
Healthray LIMS brings routine laboratory work onto a single system, covering investigations such as CBC, Lipid Profile, LFT, and KFT, while connecting analysers and other healthcare systems. It also brings billing, inventory, automation, and AI into the same workflow, along with ELN, LES, and SDMS for managing laboratory processes and data. The platform supports quality workflows, multi-centre operations, flexible deployment, data migration, and ongoing support, making it easier for labs to move from their existing system.

| Best For Growing diagnostic labs, pathology centres, hospital laboratories, and multi-branch diagnostic networks *★★★★★ 5 on Techjockey*  |
| :---- |

#### **What Stands Out**

* **Connected Lab Workflows:** Every module works from the same sample record, connecting order entry, barcode tracking, analyser results, validation, QC, billing, and QR-based report delivery without repeatedly entering the same information.  
* **Analyser & System Integration:** Supports bi-directional analyser interfacing with HL7, FHIR, EMR/EHR/HIS, and PACS/DICOM connections, making it easier to move lab data between instruments and connected healthcare systems.  
* **Quality & Accreditation Workflows:** Covers Levey-Jennings charts, Westgard rules, SOP version control, CAPA, staff competency records, equipment calibration logs, and tamper-proof audit trails for NABL/ISO-related workflows.  
* **Simpler Migration & Go-Live:** Healthray supports migration from registers or legacy lab systems, along with workflow-based staff training and implementation, with bills and reports ready to start printing.  
* **AI-Powered Lab Automation:** AI features include smart sample routing, urgent-sample prioritisation, barcode and specimen error detection, abnormal-result flagging, and voice-to-text reporting, while TAT tracking helps identify delays at each stage.  
* **Lab Inventory Management:** Helps labs keep track of the reagents and consumables they use, so staff can see what is available and manage stock without keeping inventory separately from the rest of the lab workflow.

## **How to Choose the Right Labguru Alternative**

Switching from one lab system to another is not just about finding more features. Start with the parts of your current setup that are taking extra time or creating problems. This could be sample tracking, analyser integration, billing, report management, inventory, collection centre operations, or keeping track of pending tests and reports.

Then check what the switch will involve. Ask about data migration, implementation, staff training, support, security, user access, integrations, customisation, and the total cost. It is also worth checking whether the system fits your pathology workflows, including sample processing, report approval, billing, analyser connectivity, and work from collection centres. A system can look suitable on paper but still require major changes to the way your lab works.

Before making the final decision, ask the shortlisted vendors to show the software using situations from your own lab. Try common tasks such as registering a sample, checking its status, receiving analyser results, reviewing a report, and tracking pending tests. Also check whether the system can keep up as you add more samples, analysers, collection centres, referring doctors, or locations.

## **Making the Switch from Labguru**

Finding a Labguru alternative usually starts with looking at what is becoming difficult in your lab. It could be keeping track of samples, following pending tests, managing inventory, checking analyser results, or handling work from different branches and collection centres.

The five alternatives compared above take different approaches to lab management. Before picking one, see how each system handles the work your lab does every day. A good demo should make it clear whether the software fits your existing workflow or leaves staff with more steps to manage.

Healthray is one option to evaluate for connected workflows, analyser and system integrations, quality management, migration support, and multi-centre operations. The final decision comes down to the areas your lab needs to improve and the way you want those workflows to work.

## **FAQ’s**

### **Will I still have access to my Labguru data after switching?**

Check Labguru’s data-export and account-termination terms before you move. It is also worth confirming the format of the exported data and how long you can access it after the account is closed.

### **How much downtime can a lab expect when switching from Labguru?**

There is no fixed timeline for the switch. Labs with more data and connected systems may need more time, especially when setup, testing, and staff training are involved. Ask the vendor how they plan to keep your regular lab work running during the changeover.

### **Can we switch to a new LIMS in stages?**

Yes, a phased move may be possible. A lab with several teams, projects, or locations can discuss starting with one area first and moving the rest once the new setup is working properly.

### **Will our existing instruments work with the new LIMS?**

Do not rely only on a vendor’s general integration list. Share the exact instruments and interfaces used in your lab and ask the vendor to confirm whether they can connect and transfer data as expected.
